name: Retrieval Ratchet
tagline: Deterministic retrieval eval that gates merges in CI
summary: Retrieval Ratchet makes retrieval quality a merge gate for RAG applications. A seeded generator derives QA sets from the corpus itself with no LLM calls, a pluggable retriever protocol feeds a metric engine computing recall@k, MRR, precision@k, and lexically-grounded faithfulness, and `check` exits non-zero when results fall below a checked-in baseline. It runs offline in seconds inside GitHub Actions, with byte-identical QA output for a given seed.
highlights: Seeded synthetic-QA generator derives questions from the corpus itself — no LLM calls, byte-identical output per seed.
Metric engine computes recall@k, MRR, precision@k, and lexically-grounded faithfulness, stable run-to-run.
Regression gate compares against a checked-in baseline with float-noise tolerance; the exit code is the merge gate.
Retriever protocol needs only retrieve(query, k); TF-IDF and HTTP adapters pass a shared contract suite covering determinism and unicode queries.

name: PlanLens
tagline: Postgres plan analysis in-browser: hotspot tree + index DDL
summary: PlanLens turns a pasted Postgres EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, FORMAT JSON) plan into an interactive tree with per-node timing, ranked findings and copyable CREATE INDEX DDL. Hotspots are ranked by exclusive time, misestimation magnitude and sort/hash spills, and index suggestions derive from filters, sort keys and join conditions, each with a rationale and a check-with-EXPLAIN caveat. Parsing, analysis and share links run entirely client-side, so plans containing real data never leave the machine.
highlights: Normalizes 50+ node types into a tree; exclusive time is derived by subtracting children's inclusive time.
Quantifies row-estimate drift per node as a signed log ratio between planner estimate and actual rows.
Generates CREATE INDEX DDL with equality-before-range-before-sort column order, partial and expression indexes, and prefix deduplication.
Flags filtered Seq Scans, sort and hash spills, dead branches, nested-loop misestimates, and trigger or JIT time.
